title: Claim
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/pools/claim, application/json, with which the starter claims a request for one machine. The control plane queues work in each workspace, and a claim by one of that workspace's node pools takes the work the control plane chooses for that node pool. Without pool_id the claim covers the key's node pool, definitions.schema.json; with a pool_id that is not the key's node pool, the claim is refused, 403 forbidden, the same as an unknown one. The control plane holds the request up to wait_seconds while the claim can take no work, because none that it may take waits in its workspace's queue or the key's node pool is at its instance limit, and answers a signed 200 with claim-answer.schema.json when work can be claimed within that time, or a signed 204 with no body at its end. Each claimed dispatch takes a slot of the node pool's instance limit at the claim. A machine event of a dispatch is an accepted dispatched, dispatched.schema.json, the machine's redemption of the dispatch's run code at the enrolment, https://qory.dev/contracts/forager/v1/enrolment.schema.json, or an accepted machine end in any state, machine-end.schema.json. A machine log, machine-log.schema.json, is not a machine event. Until the first machine event of the dispatch, the slot is freed once, at the first of these: the release of the dispatch, release.schema.json; the lapse of its lease, claim-answer.schema.json; or the end of the dispatch for any reason, such as when the machine has not redeemed the run code within 15 minutes of the claim, or when the control plane ends the work it is for. The lapse of the lease makes the dispatch stale when neither dispatched nor the redemption of its run code came before lease_until. So a stale dispatch keeps no slot until its first machine event, though it has not ended, unless a refused dispatched or redemption took its slot again. From the first machine event on, the release, the lapse of the lease and the end of the dispatch free no slot until the control plane accepts a machine end with the state gone for the dispatch. A dispatched accepted for a live dispatch takes no slot. A refusal takes a slot again in two cases. The first is a dispatched refused 409 lease_expired or 410 gone, dispatched.schema.json. The second is a refused redemption of the run code at the enrolment, https://qory.dev/contracts/forager/v1/enrolment.schema.json, for which all of these are true. Its proof verifies under its public_key. The gateway that the run code is bound to, claim-answer.schema.json, relayed it. No redemption of the run code was accepted before. It is refused because the run code expired, the run ended, or the dispatch is stale or ended. The control plane still has the run code. A refused redemption gets the same answer as an unknown code, the unsigned 401 of that contract. When the work is closed or undone, the control plane deletes the run code, so a later redemption takes no slot, while a refused dispatched still takes one. A redemption whose proof does not verify, or that a gateway other than the bound one relays, takes no slot and does not move the time limit for a slot. A later accepted machine end other than gone, or such a refusal, takes a freed slot again until the control plane accepts gone, even when the node pool is then over its instance limit. Such a machine end still gets the signed 204. An accepted gone frees the slot once the dispatch has ended or is stale, whether or not dispatched or a machine end with the state deleting came first. Until then, the dispatch keeps the slot, and the slot is freed when the dispatch ends or goes stale. An accepted gone never takes a slot: when gone comes after the slot was freed, also as the first machine event of the dispatch, the slot stays free. After an accepted gone, no call takes the slot again, whether the call is accepted or refused. The control plane has a time limit for a slot: it frees the slot that a dispatch keeps once max_lifetime_minutes, claim-answer.schema.json, plus 60 minutes have passed since the start of the limit. The limit starts at the latest of the claim, the first accepted dispatched, the first accepted redemption of the run code, the last accepted machine end, and the last refusal that took the slot again. The claim matters only when the dispatch has none of the others. A dispatched or a redemption sent again does not move the time limit, because only the first accepted one counts. A starter can rely on the time limit for a slot even when its gone never arrives. Every accepted machine end gets the signed 204 with no body. So does a gone after a gone, and a gone after the time limit for a slot freed the slot. A claim is refused, 409 no_gateway, when the choice of the key's node pool resolves to no gateway. It is signed with the pool's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the starter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

pool_id.description: The key's node pool, an optional check: any other value is refused, 403 forbidden.

wait_seconds.description: How long the control plane may hold the request while no work can be claimed, in seconds, from 0 to 25: 0 answers at once.

offers.description: The machines the pool can create, 1 to 64 of them: for each, disk_gib is the largest disk the pool gives that machine. The control plane gives a claim with offers only work for a run whose machine type one of the offers fits, definitions.schema.json. A claim without offers gets only work for a run of the instance's default machine type. An answer to a claim with offers has machine and machine_spec, and an answer to a claim without offers has neither. A provisioner that uses a machine adapter claims only after a successful check of the adapter, and sends the offers of the adapter's last successful check, so each of its claims has offers, https://qory.dev/contracts/machines/v1/check-answer.schema.json.
